question: Using logarithmic differentiation, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ if $$y=x^{\log x},\qquad x>0.$$
explanation:
Taking logarithm
$$\log y=\log x\cdot\log x=(\log x)^2.$$
Differentiation
$$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=2\log x\cdot\frac{1}{x}=\frac{2\log x}{x}.$$
Substitution of the original function
Since $y=x^{\log x}$, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=x^{\log x}\frac{2\log x}{x}.$$
Thus, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=2x^{\log x-1}\log x.$$
